messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] keplermed-prod-dedicated pool GPU utilization 97% for 3m, request queue 420, 503 spike rate 18% — paging @jamal_oncall and @maria_sre
jamal_oncall: ack, I'm up. looking now. any customer impact reports?
maria_sre: seeing increased latency on /v1/chat/generate for tenant keplermed — p95 ~4.2s -> 12s, p99 ~18s. errors are mostly enqueue/timeouts.
tanya_se: also seeing KV cache miss rate jump for keplermed, looks like cold-cache after a burst of long-context requests.
jamal_oncall: ok. can we get pool-level metrics + model queue tails?
ops_bot: metrics link: https://console.redwood/metrics/pools/keplermed-prod — gpu-util=97%, queued_requests=423, avg_kv_miss=42%
infra_ankit: verified. Autoscale policy spikes at 100% but region has only limited spare capacity — we can attempt emergency burst (if allowed) or fall back to smaller quantized model.
jamal_oncall: what's impact to other tenants if we burst? any risk of eviction?
infra_ankit: burst will allocate reserved spare GPUs in the region; risk: short-lived throttles to best-effort tenants. No evictions for dedicated pools.
maria_sre: customer SLAs: keplermed has enterprise SLA 99.9, high priority. recommend: 1) request emergency burst 2) deploy canary to route % of traffic to quantized-ggml-8bit model (same topology) for latency relief 3) enable prefix caching for recent prompts
jamal_oncall: can we do both now? burst + canary? time-sensitive.
infra_ankit: we can run burst command in ~2m. Canary deploy can be done via routing rule change — need product approval for model fallback.
accountmgr_jess: notifying KeplerMed support channel now. tagging their on-call (keplermed_support).
keplermed_support: seeing increased 5xx, some user-facing timeouts. Please advise, this is impacting search -> triage queues.
jamal_oncall: decision: approve emergency burst + canary fallback (20% -> 50% if healthy). I'm taking lead.
maria_sre: documenting actions. Runbook ref: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-pool-exhaustion#keplermed
jamal_oncall: infra_ankit, please execute burst command. Keep duration short (30m) and we will monitor.
infra_ankit: executing now. command:
```
redwoodctl pools burst --pool keplermed-prod --add-gpus 4 --duration 30m --reason "Prod: keplermed gpu saturation emergency"
```
infra_ankit: burst request submitted, request_id=brst-2159994321-ankit. provisioning...
ops_bot: provisioning started — expected available in ~90s
maria_sre: in parallel deploying routing change: route 20% traffic to quantized-ggml-8bit-canary for tenants/keplermed/model/chat-main.
tanya_se: rolling canary: 1) start 20% 2) watch p50/p95 errors 3) if stable, increment to 50%
infra_ankit: burst completed, new GPUs attached. pool gpu-util now 58% (after inflight queue drained).
ops_bot: metrics update: queued_requests down 42% -> 240, 5xx rate down to 6%
keplermed_support: confirming — our dashboards show user-facing latencies improving. thank you.
accountmgr_jess: emailed KeplerMed escalation contact with summary and expected recovery timeline.
maria_sre: after 10m canary looks good (p95 down to 3.1s, 5xx ~2%). increasing canary to 50% per plan.
jamal_oncall: good. keep burst for 30m, monitor. post-incident we'll propose config changes: larger baseline for night windows and prefix caching config.
infra_ankit: setting auto-release timer for burst at 30m. Will escalate if capacity still high.
ops_bot: scheduled tear-down at +30m unless cancelled.
jamal_oncall: handoff to maria for post-incident analysis. I'm on standby for questions.
maria_sre: will open incident report and assign action items (model routing safety net, autoscale headroom request for region, runbook clearer thresholds).
keplermed_support: thanks team — we've resumed normal ops. will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
jamal_oncall: resolved for now. closing active paging but keeping thread open for notes.
